stem.en:
When water becomes unavailable, tardigrades, tiny animals that live in moss, soil, and fresh water, do not simply dry up and die. Instead, they draw in their legs and shrink into a dried form called a "tun." In this state their metabolism is suspended, and they can go without food or water for years. When water returns, they rehydrate and become active again.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Tardigrades survive long dry periods by entering a dried, inactive state.
Tardigrades need a constant supply of fresh water in order to stay alive.
Tardigrades grow much larger after they are rehydrated following a dry period.
Tardigrades leave their homes to search for water when the moss dries out.

why.en: The text explains how tardigrades form a dried 'tun', stop their metabolism and revive with water: that is how they survive dry periods.
why.uz: Matn tardigradlar qanday qilib quruq «tun» holatiga oʻtishi, metabolizmni toʻxtatishi va suv bilan qayta tirilishini tushuntiradi.
why.ru: Текст объясняет, как тихоходки сворачиваются в сухой «tun», останавливают обмен веществ и оживают с водой: так они переживают засуху.

stem.en:
The following text is from a short story. Malika has recently moved to a new city.

For the first weeks, Malika walked to school along the main road, eyes fixed on the pavement. The city seemed to belong to everyone but her. Then one morning a baker, sweeping the step of his shop, nodded and called out, "Good morning, girl with the green bag!" It was a small thing. Still, the next day Malika chose the same street, and the day after that, she found herself looking up.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: A small act of recognition begins to make a newcomer feel at home.
A newcomer changes her route to school to avoid a busy main road.
A shop owner tries to persuade a new student to buy his bread every day.
A student loses her green bag on her way to school one morning.

why.en: Malika feels like an outsider until a baker greets her; afterward she returns to his street and starts 'looking up', a sign she feels more at home.
why.uz: Malika oʻzini begona his qiladi, soʻng novvoy u bilan salomlashadi; keyin u oʻsha koʻchadan yuradi va «looking up», yaʼni oʻzini erkinroq his qiladi.
why.ru: Малика чувствует себя чужой, пока пекарь её не приветствует; потом она ходит по его улице и «looking up», то есть осваивается.

stem.en:
The scholar al-Biruni, born in 973 in Kath, in the region of Khwarazm, used an inventive method to calculate the radius of the Earth. First he measured the height of a hill. Then, standing on its top, he measured how far the horizon appeared to dip below a level line of sight. Using trigonometry, he calculated the Earth's radius from these two measurements.

According to the text, which two measurements did al-Biruni use to calculate the Earth's radius?

options.en: The height of a hill and the dip of the horizon seen from its top
The distance between two cities and the angle of the Sun at noon in each
The length of a day and the time the Moon takes to orbit the Earth
The width of a valley and the height of the mountains around it

why.en: The text names exactly two measurements: the hill's height and how far the horizon dipped as seen from the top.
why.uz: Matnda aniq ikki oʻlchov aytilgan: tepalikning balandligi va uning choʻqqisidan qaraganda ufqning qancha pastga tushishi.
why.ru: В тексте названы ровно два измерения: высота холма и то, насколько опускается горизонт, если смотреть с его вершины.

stem.en:
Members of a school chess club noticed that students who joined the club in the autumn seemed to do better on their math tests by spring. Sardor, the club leader, suggested that playing chess regularly improves students' ability to solve math problems. A teacher pointed out, however, that the students who chose to join the club might already have been stronger in math.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Sardor's suggestion?

options.en: Before joining, club members already had higher math scores than other students.
Club members played chess for at least two hours each week during the year.
Club members said that they enjoyed chess more than any other school activity.
Club members improved even further in math by the end of the following school year.

why.en: If members were already better at math before joining, their good scores need not come from chess, which is the teacher's point.
why.uz: Agar aʼzolar klubga kirishdan oldin ham matematikada kuchliroq boʻlsa, ularning yaxshi natijasi shaxmatdan kelmagan boʻlishi mumkin.
why.ru: Если участники были сильнее в математике ещё до вступления в клуб, их хорошие оценки могут быть вовсе не от шахмат.

stem.en:
In a poem, the speaker suggests that the river near her village changes with the seasons while remaining, in some way, the same.

Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates this claim?

options.en: "In spring it roars, in August it barely whispers, / yet every year it finds the same old bend."
"My father fished there every morning, / and taught me how to cast a line."
"The village children race their paper boats / and shout whenever one goes under."
"Beyond the river lies the road to the city, / which none of us has ever traveled."

why.en: The claim has two parts. 'Roars' and 'barely whispers' show change; 'the same old bend' shows what stays the same. No other line shows both.
why.uz: Fikr ikki qismdan iborat: «roars» va «barely whispers» oʻzgarishni, «the same old bend» esa oʻzgarmas narsani koʻrsatadi. Boshqa satrlarda ikkalasi yoʻq.
why.ru: У утверждения две части: «roars» и «barely whispers» показывают перемены, «the same old bend» — то, что не меняется. Других строк с обоими нет.

stem.en:
In a class experiment, a student recorded how long four kinds of seeds took to sprout. Radishes and carrots were the two root vegetables tested.

Seed | Average days to sprout
Radish | 4
Lettuce | 7
Pepper | 12
Carrot | 15

The student claims that, among the seeds tested, root vegetables did not always sprout faster than other vegetables.

Which choice best uses data from the table to support the student's claim?

options.en: Carrot seeds took 15 days to sprout, longer than both lettuce (7) and pepper (12) seeds.
Radish seeds sprouted in 4 days, faster than any other seed that was tested.
Lettuce seeds took 7 days to sprout, 5 days fewer than pepper seeds took.
Pepper and carrot seeds took a combined total of 27 days to sprout.

why.en: Carrot is a root vegetable that sprouted slower than two non-root vegetables, so root vegetables were not always faster. Radish shows the opposite.
why.uz: Sabzi ildizmevali sabzavot, lekin ikki boshqa sabzavotdan sekinroq unib chiqqan, demak ildizmevalilar har doim tezroq emas. Turp esa aksini koʻrsatadi.
why.ru: Морковь — корнеплод, но взошла медленнее двух некорнеплодов, значит, корнеплоды не всегда быстрее. Редис показывает обратное.

stem.en:
A school library tracked how many books students borrowed each month in two categories.

Month | Fiction | Nonfiction
September | 140 | 60
October | 150 | 90
November | 145 | 125

The librarian noticed that although fiction remained more popular each month, ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

options.en: the number of nonfiction books borrowed more than doubled from September to November.
the number of fiction books borrowed fell sharply from September to November.
students borrowed more nonfiction books than fiction books during the month of October.
the number of nonfiction books borrowed stayed the same each month.

why.en: Nonfiction went from 60 to 125, more than double. Fiction rose slightly (140 to 145), and nonfiction never passed fiction.
why.uz: Ilmiy-ommabop kitoblar 60 tadan 125 taga yetdi, bu ikki baravardan koʻp. Badiiy kitoblar biroz oshdi (140 dan 145 ga).
why.ru: Научно-популярные книги выросли с 60 до 125, больше чем вдвое. Художественные немного выросли (со 140 до 145) и всегда оставались впереди.

stem.en:
Every year, the gardeners at a city park plant the same flowerbed with red tulips. This spring, half of the bed bloomed red as usual, but the other half produced yellow flowers. The head gardener checked the delivery records and found that the bulbs for that half had come from a different supplier than in previous years. The gardener concluded that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: the new supplier had probably sent a different variety of tulip bulb.
the soil in that part of the park had slowly turned the red tulips yellow.
the yellow flowers had been planted in secret by visitors to the park.
the gardeners had forgotten to water that half of the flowerbed.

why.en: Only the yellow half came from a new supplier, so the most logical explanation is that this supplier sent a different kind of bulb.
why.uz: Faqat sariq gullagan yarmi yangi yetkazib beruvchidan kelgan, demak eng mantiqiy izoh: u boshqa navdagi piyozboshlarni yuborgan.
why.ru: Только жёлтая половина пришла от нового поставщика, значит, логичнее всего, что он прислал луковицы другого сорта.

stem.en:
Wild apple trees of the species Malus sieversii grow in the mountains of Central Asia, including the Tian Shan. A 2010 DNA analysis identified this species as the primary ancestor of the domesticated apple. If this is correct, the apples sold in markets around the world today ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: are descended mainly from wild trees of Central Asia.
were first grown from seeds that were found in Europe.
will soon be replaced in markets by wild Central Asian apples.
no longer share any traits with Malus sieversii.

why.en: If the wild Central Asian species is the main ancestor of the domesticated apple, today's apples descend mainly from those wild trees.
why.uz: Agar Markaziy Osiyo yovvoyi olmasi madaniy olmaning asosiy ajdodi boʻlsa, bugungi olmalar asosan oʻsha yovvoyi daraxtlardan kelib chiqqan.
why.ru: Если дикая среднеазиатская яблоня — главный предок культурной, то нынешние яблоки происходят в основном от этих диких деревьев.

stem.en:
Ozoda noticed that her town's swimming pool was nearly empty on weekday afternoons but overcrowded on weekends. She suggested to the pool's manager that tickets for weekday afternoons be sold at half price. If the manager adopts her plan and it works as Ozoda intends, the pool will most likely ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: draw more weekday afternoon visitors and smaller weekend crowds.
earn much more money from weekend visitors than it does at present.
close earlier on weekday afternoons than it does now.
need to raise the price of its weekend tickets.

why.en: Cheaper weekday tickets are meant to move swimmers from crowded weekends to empty weekday afternoons, spreading visitors more evenly.
why.uz: Arzon ish kuni chiptalari suzuvchilarni gavjum dam olish kunlaridan boʻsh ish kunlariga oʻtkazish uchun moʻljallangan.
why.ru: Дешёвые билеты в будни должны перевести посетителей с переполненных выходных на пустые будние дни.

stem.en:
Ibn Sina, born around 980 in the village of Afshana near Bukhara, wrote The Canon of Medicine, a five-volume encyclopedia that gathered the medical knowledge of his time into a single, ordered system. For centuries afterward, the Canon served as a standard medical textbook in both the Islamic world and Europe. Its long use suggests that its value may have lain less in any single fact it recorded than in the way it organized knowledge, giving students a framework into which new findings could be placed.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: The Canon's lasting importance may have come from how it organized medical knowledge, not only from what it contained.
The Canon was used as a textbook in Europe only after later physicians had rewritten and reordered all five of its volumes.
The Canon of Medicine was the first book ever written about medicine.
Ibn Sina is better known for his birthplace near Bukhara than for his writing.

why.en: The last sentence carries the main idea: the Canon lasted because of its organizing framework, not just its individual facts.
why.uz: Asosiy gʻoya oxirgi gapda: «Tib qonunlari» alohida faktlar tufayli emas, balki bilimni tartibga solgan tizimi tufayli uzoq yashagan.
why.ru: Главная мысль — в последнем предложении: «Канон» жил долго благодаря своей системе, упорядочившей знания, а не только отдельным фактам.

stem.en:
The following text is from a short story. Timur is visiting the apartment where he grew up, which now belongs to another family.

The new owners had painted the kitchen white and moved the table to the window, and Timur, standing in the doorway, felt a flash of something like offense. Then he noticed the doorframe where his mother had once marked his height on each birthday, the pencil lines faint now but still there, unpainted, as though someone had decided to leave them. He found that he could not decide whether that small mercy made the room easier or harder to leave.

Which choice best describes Timur's feelings in the text?

options.en: He is unsettled by the changes and torn when he finds a trace of his past preserved.
He is pleased that the new owners have made the old kitchen brighter and more modern.
He is angry that the new owners have erased every sign that his family lived there.
He is indifferent to the apartment and eager to leave it as quickly as possible.

why.en: He feels 'something like offense' at the changes, then cannot decide if the saved pencil marks make leaving easier or harder: he is torn.
why.uz: Oʻzgarishlarni koʻrib «something like offense» his qiladi, soʻng saqlangan belgilar ketishni osonlashtiradimi yoki qiyinlashtiradimi, hal qila olmaydi.
why.ru: Перемены вызывают у него «something like offense», а затем он не может решить, легче или тяжелее уйти из-за сохранённых отметок: он в смятении.

stem.en:
It is tempting to judge a city's public transport by speed alone: how quickly a bus or train can carry a passenger from one end of the city to the other. But for many riders, the more important measure is frequency. A fast train that comes once an hour may serve a commuter worse than a slower bus that comes every five minutes, because the time spent waiting, often in the cold or the heat, counts as much in a traveler's day as the time spent moving.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: How often a service runs can matter more to riders than how fast it travels.
Trains are generally a better form of public transport than buses are.
Cities should build faster trains to cut the time that passengers spend moving.
Most riders would rather wait indoors than outdoors for public transport.

why.en: The text argues that 'frequency' can matter more than speed, because waiting time counts as much as travel time.
why.uz: Matnda «frequency», yaʼni qatnov tezligi emas, balki qanchalik tez-tez kelishi muhimroq boʻlishi mumkinligi isbotlanadi: kutish vaqti ham hisobga kiradi.
why.ru: Текст доказывает, что «frequency» (частота) может быть важнее скорости, ведь время ожидания тоже входит в день пассажира.

stem.en:
A student is writing an essay about a short story in which the narrator returns to her hometown. The student claims that by the end of the story, the narrator's resentment of the town has given way to a reluctant affection for it.

Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates the student's claim?

options.en: "I had spent years complaining about its dusty streets, and yet, leaving, I caught myself memorizing them."
"The streets were as dusty as ever, and the shops still closed at noon, just as they always had."
"I had always loved the town, and I knew that I always would, wherever my life might take me."
"I left without looking back, glad to see the last of its dusty streets and its sleepy shops."

why.en: The claim needs a change from resentment to unwilling fondness. Only the first quotation has both: years of complaining, then 'memorizing' the streets.
why.uz: Fikr norozilikdan istamaygina mehrga oʻtishni talab qiladi. Ikkalasi faqat birinchi iqtibosda bor: yillab shikoyat, soʻng koʻchalarni «memorizing».
why.ru: Нужен переход от неприязни к невольной привязанности. Оба есть только в первой цитате: годы жалоб, а затем она «memorizing» улицы.

stem.en:
For a science project, Laylo found that water in a black cup warmed faster in sunlight than water in an otherwise identical white cup. She hypothesizes that this happened because the black surface absorbs more of the sunlight, rather than because of some other difference between the cups.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Laylo's hypothesis?

options.en: When both cups were placed in a dark room warmer than the water, the water in each warmed at the same rate.
When both cups were placed in sunlight again the following day, the water in the black cup again warmed faster.
When the cups were weighed, the black cup turned out to be noticeably heavier than the white cup.
When Laylo asked her classmates, most of them predicted that the white cup would warm faster.

why.en: Without sunlight the cups behave the same, so the difference must come from sunlight. Repeating the test shows the effect again but not its cause.
why.uz: Quyosh nurisiz stakanlar bir xil isiydi, demak farq aynan quyosh nuridan. Tajribani takrorlash natijani yana koʻrsatadi, lekin sababini emas.
why.ru: Без солнечного света стаканы греются одинаково, значит, разница — от солнца. Повтор опыта снова показывает эффект, но не его причину.

stem.en:
A youth sports center recorded the number of teenagers who signed up for three programs in two years.

Program | 2024 sign-ups | 2025 sign-ups
Football | 180 | 190
Basketball | 60 | 90
Volleyball | 40 | 70

The center's director claims that, measured as a percentage, sign-ups grew far more in volleyball than in football from 2024 to 2025.

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the director's claim?

options.en: Volleyball sign-ups rose by 30, a 75% increase, while football sign-ups rose by 10, an increase of about 6%.
Football had more sign-ups than volleyball in both 2024 and 2025.
Basketball and volleyball sign-ups each rose by 30 from 2024 to 2025.
Football sign-ups rose from 180 to 190, the largest number of sign-ups in either year.

why.en: The claim is about percentage growth: 30 of 40 is 75%, while 10 of 180 is about 6%. Only the first choice compares the two percentages.
why.uz: Gap foizdagi oʻsish haqida: 40 dan 30 ga oʻsish 75%, 180 dan 10 ga oʻsish esa taxminan 6%. Faqat birinchi javob ikkala foizni solishtiradi.
why.ru: Речь о росте в процентах: +30 к 40 — это 75%, а +10 к 180 — около 6%. Только первый ответ сравнивает эти проценты.

stem.en:
For a class project, students recorded the average hours of sleep reported by students in each grade at their school and each grade's average score on a short memory quiz.

Grade | Average hours of sleep | Average quiz score (out of 20)
9 | 7.8 | 15
10 | 7.1 | 14
11 | 6.4 | 12
12 | 6.0 | 13

A student argues that in these data less sleep tends to go with lower quiz scores, but that the pattern is not perfectly consistent.

Which choice best describes data from the table that support the student's argument?

options.en: Scores fall as sleep falls from grade 9 to grade 11, but grade 12 slept least and outscored grade 11.
Grade 9 students slept the most and had the highest average quiz score of any grade.
Students in every grade averaged fewer than 8 hours of sleep per night.
Average quiz scores fell steadily from grade 9 all the way through grade 12.

why.en: The argument has two parts: a general trend (grades 9-11) and an exception (grade 12 slept least but scored 13, above grade 11's 12).
why.uz: Daʼvo ikki qismli: umumiy tendensiya (9-11-sinflar) va istisno (12-sinf eng kam uxlagan, lekin 13 ball olgan, 11-sinfning 12 balidan yuqori).
why.ru: У утверждения две части: общая тенденция (9-11 классы) и исключение (12 класс спал меньше всех, но набрал 13, больше, чем 12 у 11 класса).

stem.en:
A lichen is not a single organism but a partnership: algae or cyanobacteria live among the threads of a fungus, and through photosynthesis they produce sugars that feed both partners. The fungus benefits from these carbohydrates. Lichens are found on bare rock, on walls, and on exposed soil. On a bare rock, then, the fungal partner in a lichen most likely gets its carbohydrates mainly from ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: the algae or cyanobacteria that live among its threads.
the minerals in the rock on which the lichen is growing.
other fungi growing on the same rock nearby.
rainwater that collects on the surface of the rock.

why.en: The text says the photosynthetic partner makes the sugars and the fungus benefits from them, so the fungus's food comes from that partner.
why.uz: Matnga koʻra shakarni fotosintez qiluvchi hamkor ishlab chiqaradi va zamburugʻ undan foydalanadi, demak zamburugʻning ozuqasi oʻsha hamkordan.
why.ru: По тексту сахара производит фотосинтезирующий партнёр, а гриб их получает, значит, пища гриба поступает от этого партнёра.

facts.claim: A lichen is a composite organism of algae or cyanobacteria living among fungal filaments in a mutually beneficial relationship.
The algal or cyanobacterial partner makes sugars by photosynthesis that feed both partners; the fungi benefit from these carbohydrates.
Lichens grow on rock, walls and exposed soil.

stem.en:
When a town replaced the streetlights on its main road with brighter ones, residents expected fewer late-night accidents. Over the next year, the number of accidents on that road did fall. In the same year, however, the town also lowered the speed limit on the road and added a new pedestrian crossing. Because of these other changes, the drop in accidents ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: cannot be credited to the brighter lights alone.
proves that brighter streetlights prevent road accidents.
shows that the lower speed limit had no effect on drivers.
must have been caused by the new pedestrian crossing.

why.en: Three changes happened at once, so the fall in accidents cannot be assigned to any single one of them, including the lights.
why.uz: Bir vaqtda uchta oʻzgarish boʻlgan, shuning uchun baxtsiz hodisalar kamayishini ulardan faqat bittasiga, jumladan chiroqlarga bogʻlab boʻlmaydi.
why.ru: Одновременно произошли три изменения, поэтому снижение аварий нельзя приписать какому-то одному из них, в том числе фонарям.

stem.en:
An octopus has three hearts. One pumps blood around the body, while the other two pump blood through the gills. Octopus blood carries oxygen with the help of haemocyanin, a copper-rich protein that gives the blood a bluish color. If a student learns that a newly described sea animal also has bluish blood, the student might reasonably suspect, though not conclude, that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: its blood also carries oxygen with a copper-rich protein.
the animal must also have exactly three separate hearts of its own.
the animal is unable to take in oxygen through gills.
its blood contains no protein of any kind at all.

why.en: In the octopus the blue color comes from a copper-rich oxygen carrier, so blue blood is a reasonable clue, not proof, of a similar protein.
why.uz: Sakkizoyoqda koʻk rang mis saqlovchi kislorod tashuvchi oqsildan keladi, shuning uchun koʻk qon oʻxshash oqsilga ishora, lekin isbot emas.
why.ru: У осьминога синий цвет даёт медьсодержащий переносчик кислорода, поэтому синяя кровь — разумный намёк на похожий белок, но не доказательство.
